newsitem.title: INDIA: WEEK AHEAD-Indian shares seen consolidating gains.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Indian shares seen consolidating gains.

text.p: Revival of domestic institutional demand is expected to help Indian shares consolidate gains this week, brokers said.
"The outlook is positive. I expect domestic institutional participation to supplement foreign fund buying," said broker Maulik Sharedalal at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Fresh demand is seen chiefly coming from Unit Trust of India (UTI), the country's largest mutual fund, which collected about 20 billion rupees in July through the sale of units, traders said.
"One of the main factors for the stocks rally was because the UTI had stopped selling," said Rasesh Maniar, a dealer at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd. "We expect UTI to become a net buyer this year."
Last week the BSE's benchmark 30-share index jumped 157.51 points, or 3.76 percent, to 4,347.32.
Analysts said the market was being driven by expectations of economic revival in the second half of 1997/98 (April-March) after a slowdown hit demand and squeezed company profits.

"Even though the industry took 18-20 months to recover after the FY92 (financial year ended March 31, 1992) recession, we believe the turnaround this time will set in within 12-14 months -- it should start in FY98 itself," Anindya Chatterjee, economist at NatWest Markets said.
"Our model suggests 9.5 percent growth in manufacturing in FY98, implying a clear turnaround from the average 3.3 percent growth in November 1996-March 1997," he said in a report.
Effective lending rates have fallen more than 300 basis points in the last 10 months, boosting liquidity and giving companies a sigh of relief, Chatterjee added.
"Rates are likely to remain soft for most of FY98, so investment and consumption demand are set to rise," he said.
Traders expect the market to trade between 4,400 points and 4,448 -- the year's high reached a few weeks ago.
"We'll see some resistance at the year's high," said Kanu Dave, a technical analyst. "I don't see it being breached -- the market will consolidate."
